body:
Agreed, see above:
> Will update the documentation after we've decided on a solution

Sorry for the long wait. In my opinion, the required return format is inconvenient from a usability perspective. When I suggested a table, I meant 4 columns and an unlimited number of rows, whereas in the current version, we have 1–4 rows and an unlimited number of columns. The table ends up transposed, which is inconvenient and likely unintuitive for the user.

Yes, your version is more memory-efficient: `1 * Array + 4 * PackedStringArray(N elements)` instead of `1 * Array + N * PackedStringArray(4 elements)`. But I don't think this is a big issue, even if the plugin processes thousands of translation strings. I would prioritize convenience and clarity in this case, but let me know if you disagree. Here's a test project for comparison: [test-translation-parser.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18851519/test-translation-parser.zip).

I would also change the column order: "messages, messages_plural, contexts, comments" looks more natural than "messages, contexts, messages_plural, comments".

Or alternatively we could replace the return type with `Dictionary[StringName, PackedStringArray]` (or just `Dictionary` for extensibility) and use named columns.
I'll look into implementing this change tomorrow
